supersedes.reason: Independent review found local-path external identifiers, caller-owned decoded aliases, Python divergence for Draft integer-valued numbers, and trailing control-character acceptance. This record preserves the original submission and binds the focused portable-contract remediation.

checks.result: Deterministic generation, strict TypeScript typecheck, and all 19 contract tests across three files pass. The exact local-path, trailing-control, immutable-snapshot, and serialized integral-number cases pass.

checks.command: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest tests.contracts.test_domain_contracts tests.foundation.test_adr_check tests.foundation.test_build_manifest tests.foundation.test_quality_check tests.foundation.test_ui_change_gate
checks.result: All 55 focused contract/foundation tests pass. Draft 2020-12 and generated Python reject Windows drive, drive-relative, UNC, POSIX absolute/home/relative, and file-URI identifier forms in observed and normalized fields; trailing CR/LF is rejected; serialized 1.0 revisions are accepted and normalized to Python int.
All 16 focused Core API tests pass, proving the generated Python hardening remains compatible with the current service boundary.
Formatting, Ruff lint, and mypy pass for all 83 governed Python files. Report SHA-256: 919a9d9a9d62d30aae131855c94360fc26372aa152ad85b30b71e4bfdedb39e0.
ADR-0013 covers all 33 protected base-to-remediation paths and the architecture contract passes. The remediation adds no persistence, lifecycle, UI, dependency, or migration scope.

Clean deterministic build identity 0.1.0+g787e501 passes with the updated governed schema/generated bytes; manifest SHA-256 is 06d514546a06fc23e2db7b937874f6c43a200e0157d93538a1f28b22a35293e9. Planning and generated views validate.

evidence: Portable external identifiers retain legitimate DOI and HTTP(S) syntax but reject local filesystem representations in both observed and normalized values under Draft, TypeScript, and Python validation.

Both decoders first create an owned bounded snapshot, validate that stable snapshot, and return deeply runtime-immutable objects and arrays. Mutating the original nested input cannot change decoded revision bytes or values.
Python now follows Draft 2020-12 and TypeScript integer semantics for finite safe integral floats and normalizes them to int in the owned snapshot.

The focused hostile matrix covers Windows drive/drive-relative/UNC, POSIX absolute/home/relative, file URI, observed/normalized fields, trailing CR/LF, caller mutation, decoded mutation, and serialized 1.0 revision/sourceRevision values.
Snapshot collection traversal fails closed above the contract's 256-item maximum before walking attacker-controlled excess entries.

The remediation changes only the schema, deterministic generator and generated artifacts, one portable parity fixture, and focused TypeScript/Python regressions. The original ADR, architecture, build inventory, service boundary, and downstream T02/T03 ownership remain unchanged.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: The remediation is confined to a protected schema and its generated decoders. The credible impacts are cross-runtime schema parity, input ownership, privacy/path rejection, service imports, generated-code quality, ADR coverage, and build inventory; each was replayed with focused checks.
verificationSelection.deferred: Complete foundation/service profiles and cross-task lifecycle, restart, migration, and end-to-end qualification remain deferred to CAP-03.S01 slice review under the repository's risk-based test policy.

reviewerDisposition.note: Re-review the four prior findings, the exact 11-file original-candidate-to-remediation range, supersession, focused checks, and unchanged T02/T03 ownership. Do not run broad profiles.
